messages.subject: Updated countriesCoarse map for Africa
messages.body_plain:
Hi Andy, hi all,

The current maps output by rworldmap are not standard at least concerning Africa, as they violate the international consensus on some territories, this consensus coming from the United Nations (see http://www.un.org/depts/Cartographic/map/profile/africa.pdf as a reference map, and also http://www.un.org/en/decolonization/nonselfgovterritories.shtml concerning specifically Western Sahara).

I corrected the countriesCoarse map concerning two territories:
- Western Sahara is a non-self governing territory separate from Morocco whose Northern border with Morocco is a straight East-to-West line at around 27.67°N
- Somaliland is not a territory separate from Somalia, as per (lack of) international recognition. It souldn't feature as separate from Somalia, and so should be no separate entry in the countriesCoarse object. This is just the North-Western part of Somalia.

Besides, I don't know if there is the possibility to use dashed borders out of SpatialPolygons objects, but we may take note of some other few facts on the continent:
- the border between Sudan and South Sudan has not been fully agreed on by both countries yet, and os is not definitive. This doesn't apply only to the Abyei peninsula (as depicted by GoogleMaps), but to the whole border;
- the border between Somalia and Ethiopia hasn't been the object of a final agreement yet,
- there is a claim of Sudan over a small territory called the Hala'ib Triangle, in the Gebel Elba, South-East corner of Egypt. The small Bir Tawil territory, right next to it and below the 22°N line, is unclaimed territory.
- there is a border dispute between South Sudan and Kenya.

Please find my modified countriesCoarse object in attachment.

Regards,
   JB

messages.subject: mapBars refuses to draw bars when first category is full of zeros
messages.subject_clean: mapBars refuses to draw bars when first category is full of zeros
messages.body_plain:
Hi Andy, hi all,

Me again! :)
I am using rworldmap version 1.3-1 and noticed an unpleasant behaviour by mapBars: it seems that when the first column pointed by nameZs is full of 0's, mapBars will refuse to draw any bar. I noticed that as soon as you put a non-zero value in this first column, everything is ok, even if other columns are full of zeros.

Below is a minimal (?) example to illustrate the bug:

dat1 = data.frame(country.ISO3 = c("SOM","MAR"), intercont = c(0,0), african = c(1,3), other = c(0,0))
spdf = joinCountryData2Map(dat1,nameJoinColumn="country.ISO3")
mapBars(spdf, nameZs=c('intercont','african','other'), mapRegion='africa', symbolSize=4)
# here rworldmap outputs correct (i.e. non-zero) calculated values for symbol scales, etc:
# symbolMaxSize= 1.64  maxSumValues= 1  symbolScale= 1.64
# BUT it doesn't draw any bar on the map, just the empty map itself

And if I put an arbitrary non-zero value in the first column pointed by nameZs (first component of the bars):

dat1[1,'intercont'] = 4
spdf = joinCountryData2Map(dat1,nameJoinColumn="country.ISO3")
mapBars(spdf, nameZs=c('intercont','african','other'), mapRegion='africa', symbolSize=4)
# now everything works fine, even though the third component "other" equals zero everywhere.

My current workaround is to preprocess my table replacing all the NAs by 0.001 instead of 0 ;)

Regards,
   JB

P.S. I have been too lazy to check whether this has already been reported elsewhere or fixed in a later release, if it is so please just tell me in a short message and I promise to inflict myself 5 days without eating any kind of chocolate, a harsh punishment for me! :)

messages.subject: better framing for Africa in setMapExtents (aka "geography is fun")
messages.subject_clean: better framing for Africa in setMapExtents (aka "geography is fun")
messages.body_plain:
Hi there,

Last message for today here...

I have been annoyed by the fact that the functions accepting "mapRegion" as an option draw a map of African that extends far too much eastwards when using mapRegion = "africa". Currently in setMapExtents we have the following:

    if ( mapRegion == 'africa' | mapRegion == 'Africa' )#2
       {we=-20;   ea=80;    so=-30;   no=30}

The reason for this 80°E could be the far-Eastern island of Rodrigues, part of Mauritius and located around coordinates (63.440410, -19.719994), while Mauritius main island is around (57.561869, -20.296022).
The Seychelles islands, also African, are at (55.482094, -4.677215), so it's west of Mauritius mainland.

As far as I know, the final justification for this 80°E could be in our inhabited "French Southern and Antarctic Lands" (http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_Southern_and_Antarctic_Lands), within which the Kerguelen islands lie around (70°13′E, 49°21′S), and the Amsterdam island, at roughly (77°33′17″E, 37°49′33″S).

Okay, geography is fun, that's true, but IMHO it's really not worth it to include these microscopic territories in the middle of the Indian Ocean when we are talking about maps of Africa... So I suggest the following code replacement in setMapExtents. That's the ones I am currently using to draw maps of my beloved continent:

    if ( mapRegion == 'africa' | mapRegion == 'Africa' )#2
       {we=-20;   ea=55;    so=-40;   no=42}

By the way, it is not absolutely clear in every detail to me how this setMapExtents function interacts with the plotting/drawing device, because I can see that e.g. when exporting to a PDF or to the "Plots" frame in Rstudio, there are clearly other factors that enable the device to extend wider in order to match the dimensions of some other frame... For instance with my "ea = 55" in setMapExtents, I always get Mauritius to be in the plot and even quite far from the margin, while its longitude is 57.56.

messages.subject: option addSizeLegend really implemented in mapBars?
messages.subject_clean: option addSizeLegend really implemented in mapBars?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Andy, hi all,

My question is rather straightforward: is the documented option addSizeLegend (by default set at TRUE) implemented in mapBars in the current CRAN release of rworldmap (1.3-1)? While I can explicitly and successfully toggle addCatLegend to F or T, nothing happens with addSizeLegend, and I can never get that legend for the size of my bars... :(

Thanks,
   JB

messages.subject: Re: mapBars refuses to draw bars when first category is full of zeros
messages.subject_clean: mapBars refuses to draw bars when first category is full of zeros
messages.body_plain:
Hi there,

On this I have investigated a little bit, because I got very weird behaviour when some of the categories are empty, and also when I changed the zeros to e.g. 1e-3.

I found out it seems it is all related to an option to mapBars called barRelative that is present in the code of the function but not in the documentation, and by default it is set to TRUE. If you set it to FALSE, everything works fine, with or without the epsilon pseudocounts. I must admit I don't really understand what that option is supposed to do, but in the meantime I corrected a possible division by zero occurring when this option is set to TRUE. See the tiny patch I provide here. But even with that it doesn't work well when at least one of the categories (nameZs) is not to be found in any location.

Hope this helps,
   JB
